## Review: Evolution Basics
<hr>
<br/>
 
* **Evolution**:

    <!-- >- change in the genetic composition of a population over generational time -->
<br/>

* **Population**: 

    >- group of individuals of the same species, occupying the same time and space, with the potential of interbreeding <span style="color: red;">(Populations are the lowest unit of evolution, Individuals DO NOT evolve)</span>
    
<br/>

* **Species**:

    >- group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding successfully
    
<br/>

* **<span style="color:blue">Evolution by Natural Selection</span>**: 

    >- Due to the struggle for existence, organisms with heritable traits that favor survival and reproduction will tend to leave more offspring than their peers, causing those traits to **increase in frequency over generations**

## Evolution by **Natural Selection**: Darwin and others
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

* **A few things need to be true for a population to adapt**

<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 55%;">

>- Individuals in a population are not identical

>- This variation among individuals is heritable

>- Individuals sometimes die before reproducing

>- Different ancestors leave different #'s of descendants

<br/>
<br/>

* **If enough change results in reproductive isolation between populations, new species *can* evolve**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:615px; WIDTH:400px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/genetic_component.jpg">

##

<div style="float: left; width:47%;">

<br/>
<br/>
<br/>


* **Ecology determines where an evolved organism can live**
    + bees require flowering plants, specific climates, and nesting habitats
    + bees are constrained by competitors, predators, parasites, and pathogens
    
<br/>

* **Evolution determines what kind of organism ecology has to work with**
    + generations of natural selection have shaped bee species to succeed under particular sets of conditions.

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:10px; LEFT:550px; WIDTH:550px; HEIGHT:700px" SRC="images/beespecies.jpg">

<hr>
**The fossil record allows us to explore ecology:evolution in deep time**

## Why does this matter for Ecology?
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

* **Survival of the fittest** is tied to organisms interacting with their environment (abiotic & biotic factors)

<br/>

>- **This term is a little misleading, should read:**
<br/>

>- **<span style="color:red">Survival of the better designed for an immediate, local environment</span>**
      + survived death
      + reproduced successfully
      + passed on more genes than the less fortunate

<br/>

>- **The components and themes of ecology matter a lot!**
      + environments are often not stable for very long
      + even when they are stable - natural selection is still occurring

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:300px; LEFT:775px; WIDTH:300px; HEIGHT:300px" SRC="images/swallowtail.jpg">

## Ecological forces drive evolution
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width:60%;">

* **Some traits of living things are 'conserved'**
    + The genes responsible for essential functions often change very little over evolutionary time because mutations would be selected against

<br/>

* **Regardless, we often seem lots of variation within a species**

<br/>

* **Traits of a species often vary over geographic ranges**
    + why?

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:675px; WIDTH:300px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/mussel.jpg">

## When species interact, co-evolution can occur
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 60%;">

**Coevolution is the process in which two interacting species reciprocally influence each other’s evolution over time.**

<br/>

* **Bats evolved echolocation to detect and capture flying insects in darkness**

<br/>

* **Many moths evolved ears that detect bat ultrasound and trigger evasive flight**

<br/>

* **Some bats evolved quieter or altered calls that make detection harder**

<br/>

* **Some moths evolved ultrasonic clicks that can interfere with echolocation**

<br/>

* **Each adaptation changes the selective pressure on the other species — a classic coevolutionary arms race**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:180px; LEFT:700px; WIDTH:375px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/mothbat.jpg">

## Coevolution can also be evolutionary partnership
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 60%;">

**Coevolution can be an evolutionary arms race—or an evolutionary partnership**

<br/>

* **Some orchids are pollinated by only one or a few orchid bee species, creating an extremely specialized partnership**

<br/>

* **This specialization can increase pollination efficiency—but it also means the orchid may be highly dependent on the presence of the right pollinator**

<br/>

https://www.youtube.com/embed/_uHJGdTgtXE

</div>

## Ecologically driven speciation
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

* **Divergent selection between different environments can lead to the creation of reproductive barriers within a species**
    + driven by differences in environment
    + driven by interactions with other species

<br/>
<br/>

* **If populations become geographically isolated, new selection pressures drive change**

<br/>

* **Eventually *may* lead to evolution of new species**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:150px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:350px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/darwinsfinch.png">

## Creating new species can happen quickly...
<hr>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:150px; LEFT:0px; WIDTH:600px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/adaptiverad2.jpg">

<div style="float: right; width: 42%;">

**Adaptive radiation =  rapid diversification of an ancestor into multiple species adapted to different ecological niches**

<br/>

* **In Lake Victoria’s cichlid fishes, a relatively small number of ancestral lineages diversified into hundreds of species over a geologically short period**

<br/>

* **Different species evolved to feeding on algae, insects, plankton, snails, other fish, or detritus.**
    + jaws, teeth, body form, behaviors, and habitat use changed separately

</div>
